message.content: {"faithfulness": 3, "specificity": 2, "actionability": 2, "clarity": 2, "structure": 2, "overall": 3, "worst_problem": "The context_only section — the one place safety matters most — is badly broken: it covers only 2-3 of the 9 outreachSafe=false claims (missing the Havdala departure, Sanaz's Iran/IDF background, Nick's cocktail-hobby claim, the $20M ARR/competitive-struggle claim, etc.), mislabels the Cisco-acquisition claim as 'UNRESOLVED' when the source claim explicitly says 'REFUTED', and lumps in zaf-140 (an outreachSafe=true claim about buying culture) as if it were an unsafe funding fact.", "best_item": "The Money & momentum section is the strongest: all three items stay within allowed fieldKeys, cite accurate dated figures ($60M Series C on 2025-12-02, $130.5M total across 4 rounds, $10-25M revenue band) with no fabrication."}
message.reasoning:
I'm cross-checking each claim against its source, verifying the buying signals, hiring data, and momentum figures line up correctly, then moving into the tools and certifications section to confirm those citations match too.

But then I catch that the "tools" section is using contact.facet.certifications, which isn't in that section's allowed field keys list at all - that's a structural violation. I trace through the "how_they_sell" section too, checking each citation against its allowed keys, and find zaf-128 (account.strategic_moves) is being used there even though it's not permitted for that section.

I also notice a bigger issue in the context_only section: the writer labels the Cisco acquisition rumor as "UNRESOLVED" when the underlying claim status is actually "REFUTED" - that's a real faithfulness error since it flips the meaning of the whole point, which was that Zafran clarified it as an investment rather than an acquisition.

Then item 2 combines the Amex Ventures claim with zaf-140, but zaf-140 is actually a safe claim about the account's ABM buying-culture motion (outreachSafe: true) - it has nothing to do with funding and shouldn't be mixed into the unsafe/context_only section at all. That's a structural problem: mislabeling a safe claim as unsafe and misdescribing its content.

I should also check which other claims are missing from context_only that actually have outreachSafe: false, like zaf-135 for the Cisco investment.

Counting up, there are nine claims marked outreachSafe: false (135, 138, 139, 142, 153, 160, 169, 170, 171), but the context_only section only covers three of them, and one of those three (140) is misclassified. That leaves several genuinely sensitive omissions - especially zaf-153 about Sanaz's Iran/IDF background and zaf-160 about Nick's personal hobby, both of which are exactly the kind of "never mention" personal/sensitive risks that should be flagged, plus the confirmed co-founder departure in zaf-171.

I'm also checking the formatting instructions for the context_only section - it just requires each unsafe fact to have a status (refuted/unresolved/confirmed) ending in "Never mention," without a specific header format requirement, so the current h2 titling is technically fine, but the coverage gap is the real problem.

The refuted rumor being mislabeled as unresolved compounds this into a real faithfulness issue on top of the missing items.

Now I'm moving to checking the contact insights, starting with the coverage of the five people listed.

Correct count, matches instruction. But I notice the h2s are all generic "X is [title]" statements rather than capturing the "most useful thing said or did" as instructed, missing out on richer details like quotes or specific achievements.

underused) despite being explicitly allowed - a real specificity failure and generic restating of title/persona rather than surfacing the "most useful thing said or did."

The sendLines also lean toward vague filler rather than concrete action - phrases like "align with growing growth and hiring momentum" or "prepare outreach" sound like generic marketing-speak rather than specific, actionable advice tied to the actual data.

I'm also noticing one sendLine literally includes copy-pasted quote fragments with mid-sentence ellipses and truncation artifacts - that's not something a marketer could paste as-is, so it clearly fails the "actually sendable" bar. And the overall body structure keeps repeating a rigid "text/text/what it means for us" pattern instead of flowing as natural paragraphs.

Checking counts now: buying_signals has 4 items (fits 3-4 range, and no contactRefs needed since no people are named), money_momentum has 3 (fits 2-3), and tools has 3 (fits 2-3 too).

But tools uses a disallowed field key, contact.facet.certifications, when only gtm_tooling_stack, primary_tech_stack, recent_post, and publications are permitted. Similarly, how_they_sell pulls from account.strategic_moves which isn't on its allowed list either. Contact_insights hits the right count of 5 matching 5 people but has weak substance, and context_only only has 2 items covering just 3 of 9 unsafe claims while also mislabeling claim status as REFUTED instead of UNRESOLVED.

I also check whether unsafe claims leaked into other sections beyond context_only. Going through each section's citations - buying_signals, money_momentum, tools, how_they_sell, and contact_insights - none of them reference the unsafe claim IDs, so there's no leakage of unsafe info into the main sections.

But there's a real faithfulness problem: mislabeling a REFUTED claim (zaf-169) as UNRESOLVED, and mischaracterizing zaf-140 as being about funding when it's actually about buying culture. This is a meaningful misrepresentation of risk status, so faithfulness should score low, around 2.

Looking at specificity now, the body text feels generic with filler phrases like "This confirms..." rather than the verbatim quotes and dates the instructions required. Checking the claims, some fields simply lack quote text to draw from, but at least one claim with an actual quote wasn't used where it could have been.

Contact insights are especially weak on specificity - just titles listed with no verbatim quotes despite rich voice data being available in the claims, which is a real gap against the "single most useful thing that person said" instruction.

Actionability suffers too: the sendlines are mostly generic filler like "tailor value messaging to address ROI" rather than concrete next steps tied to specific data, and there's even a broken/unsendable line in the packaging section. The LinkedIn article stat about Nick was a missed chance to ground outreach in something real, so I'd score actionability around a 2.

Clarity also lands around 2 - the writing is choppy and leans on corporate filler words like "indicates" and "signals," plus that broken quote line breaks the one-line requirement.

Structure has mixed results: item counts are mostly fine and contact items are correct, but two sections use disallowed field keys, and worse, the context_only section is badly incomplete, missing most of the unsafe claims and even mislabeling a safe claim as unsafe - a serious failure in the most safety-critical part of the output.

Weighing everything, the overall score should land low, around a 3, given the structural failures in the unsafe-claims section, weak specificity and actionability, and the filler-heavy clarity issues. The worst problem is clearly the incomplete and mislabeled context_only section, while the strongest part is the money and momentum section, which stays correctly scoped and uses accurate, concrete dated figures.
